Added the CLI verb viola open: one terminal window (foot) per session beside its parent, a closed flag allowlist, only claude after --, no shell, then a non-interactive wait of up to 30 s for the new session to go live.
viola open prints a human line `<name>  live  <placement>` or one --json ok document, and refuses with exit 1 codes strict-modes-failed, already-live, stale-heartbeat, pinned-hash-mismatch, terminal-not-found, not-live, internal-error, each a --json error document; two new codes terminal-not-found and not-live carry one fixed unable/hint pair each.
A word after -- other than claude alone, or a self parent, is exit 2 with a fixed usage line before any home read, log or spawn.
viola run gained two hidden flags --origin and --place; under --origin the wrapper's start runs a window step (bounded 5 s wait for its window, one Hyprland move) after the trust step and before the slots, and records a window line in the event log and a window field in the snapshot.
viola list --json and the MCP list item gain optional window and origin; the help's setup: group now lists open, run, revive, verify, plugin install; the diag-line schema gains the subject terminal and the exit details terminal-not-found and not-live.
After implement only the operator's live-reading rig script changed; R2, the live Hyprland reading, fired once and read red on the rig, and nothing is gated by it.

body_fields.fact: The command name open is occupied by viola open, the verb that starts a named wrapped claude session in a new terminal window.

viola open starts a session in a foot terminal it spawns directly with a closed argv, no shell. It accepts only its allowlisted flags (parent, role overseer, builder or worker, cwd, workspace, model, effort, json), takes claude alone after --, and waits up to 30 s for the session to go live.
open targets the workspace of the parent's recorded window first, and otherwise the window of the nearest process ancestor up to 8 levels; with neither, the window is left unplaced.
The wrapper's window step waits up to 5 s for its terminal's window, polling every 100 ms, and makes at most one move to the asked workspace.
A window's origin is self-reported through the hidden run flag --origin and is never verified.
The normalised event kinds include window, a log-only wrapper kind that does not wake a wait.

Placement words are a closed set of eight (placed, unplaced, window-unseen, unsupported, unreachable, oversize, malformed, refused), and origin words a closed set of two (cli, agent), both defined in viola-core.
The wrapper appends one window event line, with data address, workspace, placement and origin, after the launch line, and only under --origin.
The instance snapshot carries an optional window record of address, workspace, placement and origin.
In the snapshot replay, the last window line after the last launch line wins, and a later launch line clears the window.
A list item carries an optional window of address and workspace (only an address that re-parses) and an optional origin (only an origin word), on both CLI list and MCP list.

viola open exits 0 when live, 2 on usage, and 1 on strict-modes-failed, already-live, stale-heartbeat, pinned-hash-mismatch, terminal-not-found, not-live or internal-error. Its --json ok document holds name, parent, window and placement.
The process-exit details terminal-not-found and not-live and the diag subject terminal are occupied by viola open.
viola run's hidden flags --origin and --place are occupied, and --place requires --origin.
viola-state depends on viola-hyprland, whose address check is the one window-address validator, and viola depends on viola-hyprland in its release graph.

body_fields.fact: viola open <name> starts a wrapped claude session in a new foot terminal window beside its parent; its flags are a closed allowlist (--parent, --role overseer|builder|worker, --cwd, --workspace, --model, --effort, --json) and the only words allowed after -- are claude alone; no shell runs.

viola open's usage refusals are exit 2 before any home read, log, pin or spawn: a flag outside the allowlist, any program after -- other than claude alone (a fixed usage line that echoes none of the words), or a parent naming itself.
viola open exit 0 prints <name>  live  <placement> on stdout; under --json the one ok document is {"v":1,"ok":{"name","parent","window":{"address","workspace"}|null,"placement"}}.

viola open's exit-1 codes are strict-modes-failed, already-live, stale-heartbeat, pinned-hash-mismatch, terminal-not-found, not-live and internal-error, each the {"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null} document under --json.
terminal-not-found (no foot terminal found to spawn) and not-live (the opened session never came live within its 30 s bound) are new exit-1 refusal causes, each with one fixed hint.
viola open's parent defaults to the calling agent's own ViolaName, recorded with origin agent; from a plain shell there is no parent and the origin is cli.
viola run's --origin <cli|agent> and --place <N> are hidden flags absent from help; --place without --origin is a usage error; viola revive never places a window.
the placement words are a closed set of eight (placed, unplaced, window-unseen, unsupported, unreachable, oversize, malformed, refused) and the origin words a closed set of two (cli, agent).
viola open has no MCP tool and no IPC method: opening a window is a CLI-only action.

Added the CLI verb viola open: it spawns one foot terminal window running viola run for a named session beside its parent, from a closed flag allowlist, with claude the only word allowed after the double dash, and no shell.
The wrapper (viola run) gains two hidden flags, --origin and --place; under --origin it runs a new window step (span run.window) after the trust record and before the slots, then appends one window event line after the launch line and writes the window into the first snapshot.
The diag-line schema gains the spawn subject terminal and two exit-1 process-exit details, terminal-not-found and not-live; EventKind gains window (17 to 18 kinds), log-only and outside the wait wake set.
The replay recovers the window record (the last window line after the last launch wins, a launch clears it); list --json and the MCP list tool carry window and origin per item; the Hyprland seam gains its first two product callers.
After implement only the operator's R2 rig script changed; R2 fired once and read red on the rig before reaching the open, so v2-07 stays claimed gated and v2-08 is met on the fakes and by construction.

contract/run-start-events/order: under --origin the start appends one window line after the launch line in the events log.

decision/launch-line-untraced and decision/lineage-line-untraced: the new window event line is log-only product audit data, untraced the same way as the launch line.
decision/cli-manual-dispatch-span: the new verb open opens its manual dispatch span cli.open.

contract/child-spawn-log/subject and contract/process-log/child-and-probe-lifecycle: the terminal spawn writes a process-start line with subject terminal.

contract/diag-subject/hyprctl-probe and contract/parse-rejected/hyprctl-json: the Hyprland seam now has two product callers (open's parent window read and the wrapper's window step), so hyprctl-probe pairs appear in product role files, not only in tests.

body_fields.because: The chunk adds a new time bound, open's live wait, which the report places on the open verb's own run, and a11y-plan holds each time bound as a row of its own.

body_fields.name: Window wait bounds the wrapper's own start
body_fields.rule: The wrapper's window step waits at most 5 s for its terminal's window under --origin; the bound falls on the wrapper's own start, and past it the placement is window-unseen and the start goes on, never blocking, refusing or delaying a human key.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds a new time bound, the window step's wait, which the report places on the wrapper's own start, and a11y-plan holds each time bound as a row of its own.

body_fields.rule: Each hyprctl call is bounded by a compiled 5 s deadline; the bound falls on the driver (viola open's parent read and the wrapper's window step), never on the human.
body_fields.because: The Hyprland seam gains its first two product callers, so its per-call deadline now bounds product work and a11y-plan holds it as a time-bound row of its own.
